name: marketing-cards
title: Cards
description: General-purpose marketing content cards for displaying blog posts, profiles, products, podcasts, and forum threads with image, author, excerpt, price, social links, and hover-reveal content patterns.
useWhen: Displaying a collection of mixed content types on a marketing site such as blog posts, podcasts, and resource guides.
Showcasing team members, contributors, or authors in a profile card grid.
Presenting product or service offerings with image, price, and detail in an eCommerce-adjacent marketing context.
avoidWhen: Purely eCommerce product listings — use product-cards instead for better cart integration guidance.
Structured data tables where row/column comparison is needed — cards cannot replace tabular data.
The card content is too long to preview — link to a full page instead of expanding a card.
responsiveBehavior: Card grids flow from three columns on desktop to two on tablet and one on mobile. Horizontal-layout cards (side-by-side image and text) stack vertically on small screens.
accessibility: Card images must have descriptive alt text; decorative background images use empty alt or aria-hidden.
If the entire card is clickable, wrap in an <a> with aria-label containing the card title.
Hover-reveal content must also be accessible on keyboard focus — use :focus-within CSS to show the overlay.

variants.title: Title, author, avatar, excerpt, published date and reading time
variants.description: Blog-post-style card with author avatar, title, excerpt, publication date, and reading time — the standard editorial article card.
accessibility: Author avatar alt text should name the author; <time datetime> element wraps the publication date.

variants.title: Stacked with Large Image and Content
variants.description: Large featured-image card stacked above text content — for prominent post or case study previews on resource pages.
accessibility: Large image should have descriptive alt text relating to the featured content.

variants.title: Darkened Background with Content on Hover
variants.description: Image card with a dark overlay that reveals title and excerpt on hover — a cinematic style for portfolio and media collections.
accessibility: Hover-reveal content must be visible on keyboard focus via :focus-within; do not hide content from screen readers on default state.

variants.title: Bordered with Content on Hover
variants.description: Bordered card that reveals additional content or actions on hover, keeping the default state clean and minimal.
accessibility: Hidden-on-default content must be accessible on keyboard focus; avoid using visibility:hidden for interactive elements.

variants.title: Bordered with Image, Price, Content and Details
variants.description: Product-adjacent card with image, price, description, and detail attributes — for marketing showcases of physical or digital products.
accessibility: Price should be announced clearly by screen readers; use aria-label if the price format could be ambiguous.

variants.title: Image, Name, with Social Links and Project Links
variants.description: Profile card combining a headshot, name, role, social media links, and project portfolio links — for team pages and contributor showcases.
accessibility: Social links must have aria-label identifying the platform (e.g., 'Follow on Twitter'); headshot alt names the person.

variants.title: Shaped with Image and Content
variants.description: Card with a non-standard shaped image (circular, diagonal, or clipped) alongside content — for creative and lifestyle brand marketing.
accessibility: Shaped images use CSS clip-path or border-radius; the alt text still describes the content regardless of shape.

variants.title: Podcast Post
variants.description: Podcast episode card with cover art, episode number, title, and play/listen CTA — for marketing pages promoting audio content.
accessibility: Cover art alt text describes the podcast or episode topic; play button must have an aria-label indicating the episode title.

variants.title: Forum Post
variants.description: Community forum post card with author avatar, post title, excerpt, reply count, and timestamp — for community sections on marketing sites.
accessibility: Reply count and timestamp must be announced to screen readers; use <time datetime> for publication date.
